name: Greg Norman
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first professional golf tournament, the 1976 West Lakes Classic, at age 21, and added multiple professional wins including a European Tour title by age 22.
early_history_summary: Norman took up golf at age 15 after caddying for his mother, a single-figure handicap amateur, at Virginia Golf Club in Brisbane. He went from a 27 handicap to scratch in about 18 months, then worked as a trainee professional under Charlie Earp at Royal Queensland Golf Club before turning professional in 1976 and winning his first event in his fourth professional start.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and rapid skill acquisition
family_context_summary: Born in Mount Isa, Queensland to Mervin Norman, an electrical engineer, and Toini Norman, daughter of a Finnish carpenter and a low-handicap amateur golfer who taught Greg the game at age 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Toini was a single-figure handicap golfer who introduced Norman to the sport and let him caddy for her; father was an electrical engineer with no golf background.
evidence_summary: Norman started golf at 15 after caddying for his golfing mother, reaching scratch in 18 months — an exceptionally rapid ascent suggesting strong natural ability. He trained under teaching professional Charlie Earp at Royal Queensland Golf Club, who encouraged his power game. He turned professional at 21 in 1976 and won his first tournament, the West Lakes Classic, in his fourth professional start, beating established professionals by five strokes. His mother's golf background provided initial domain exposure, but his trajectory was largely self-driven through intense practice and mentorship rather than inherited advantage.
starting_point: Born to an electrical engineer father and a Finnish-descended amateur golfer mother in Mount Isa, Queensland, Australia; middle-class family.
current_position: Chairman and CEO of Greg Norman Company; resides in Florida, USA; estimated net worth ~$400M; retired from professional golf.

trajectory.event: Turned professional and won his first tournament, the West Lakes Classic in Adelaide, by five strokes.
Won his first European Tour title at the Martini International in Scotland, establishing international presence.
Won his first major championship, The Open Championship, and reached world number one ranking for the first time.
Won his second Open Championship, cementing his legacy as one of golf's greats.
Became CEO of LIV Golf Investments, leading the Saudi-backed breakaway golf league.

name: Arie Haan
milestone_by_age_26: Scored the decisive goal in the 1971 European Cup final for Ajax and was part of the squad that won three consecutive European Cups (1971-1973), multiple Eredivisie titles, and the Intercontinental Cup by age 24.
early_history_summary: Haan joined AFC Ajax in 1967 at age 19, making his official debut in May 1968. He was a footballer-student until 1970, playing only five matches in his first three years. From the 1970-71 season he became a full professional, became a regular starter, and scored in the 1971 European Cup final against Panathinaikos at Wembley.
family_context_summary: Born in Finsterwolde, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Haan joined Ajax at 19 and was part of the most dominant club team of the early 1970s, benefiting from Rinus Michels' tactical revolution and playing alongside Johan Cruyff. He was a part-time footballer-student until 1970, then became a regular starter. His goal in the 1971 European Cup final at Wembley was his breakthrough moment. The Ajax system under Michels and then Stefan Kovacs provided elite coaching, world-class teammates, and a tactical framework that maximized his versatility and stamina. Family background is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Finsterwolde, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from football management; last managed Tianjin Teda in 2015; resides in Netherlands.

trajectory.event: Scored the decisive goal in the European Cup final against Panathinaikos at Wembley, winning Ajax's first European Cup.
Won the European Cup, Eredivisie title, Dutch Cup, and Intercontinental Cup with Ajax (treble season).
Won his third consecutive European Cup with Ajax, defeating Juventus 1-0 in the final.
Played for the Netherlands national team at the 1974 FIFA World Cup, reaching the final.
Left Ajax for Anderlecht, where he continued his successful club career.
Began managerial career, eventually managing clubs and national teams across Europe and Asia.

name: Francisco J. Ayala
milestone_by_age_26: No material scientific milestone by age 26; Ayala was ordained a Dominican priest in 1960 and graduated from the University of Salamanca, but his PhD (Columbia, 1964) and first faculty position (Rockefeller University, 1967) both came after age 26.
early_history_summary: Ayala studied at the University of Salamanca in Spain and was ordained a Dominican priest in 1960. He met Theodosius Dobzhansky around 1960 and moved to Columbia University in 1961 to begin doctoral studies in genetics, completing his PhD in 1964 at age 30.
family_context_summary: Born in Madrid, Spain; nobody in his family had studied science — their interests were in business, economics, or law.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family had business/economics background, not science.
evidence_summary: Ayala's early life was shaped by his religious vocation and scientific curiosity, but his material scientific milestones came well after age 26. He was ordained as a Dominican priest in 1960 at age 26, and only began his genetics PhD at Columbia in 1961 under Dobzhansky. His PhD was completed in 1964 and his first faculty position came in 1967. No independently verifiable scientific milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Borislav Ivkov
milestone_by_age_26: Won the inaugural World Junior Chess Championship in 1951 at age 17, earned the National Master title at 16, and became a Grandmaster in 1955 at age 21 after winning major international tournaments.
early_history_summary: Ivkov became Belgrade Junior Champion at 14 and earned his National Master title at 16 by placing shared 4th-7th in the 1949 Yugoslav Championship. At 17, he won the first-ever World Junior Chess Championship in Birmingham in 1951. He continued with strong international results and earned the Grandmaster title in 1955 after winning tournaments at Mar del Plata and Buenos Aires.
family_context_summary: Born in Belgrade, Yugoslavia (now Serbia); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Ivkov was a chess prodigy in Belgrade, becoming junior champion at 14 and national master at 16 in the strong Yugoslav chess ecosystem. His victory at the inaugural World Junior Championship at 17 was a landmark achievement. Yugoslavia was one of the world's strongest chess nations, providing competitive tournament access and peers like Svetozar Gligoric. He earned the Grandmaster title in 1955 at 21, making him one of the world's elite players. Family background is not documented, but his trajectory suggests intense self-driven practice from a young age.
starting_point: Born in Belgrade, Yugoslavia (now Serbia); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died February 14, 2022 at age 88 in Belgrade; final role: retired chess grandmaster and three-time Yugoslav Champion.

trajectory.event: Earned National Master title by placing shared 4th-7th in the Yugoslav Championship at Zagreb.
Won the inaugural World Junior Chess Championship in Birmingham, England.
Earned the Grandmaster title after winning major tournaments at Mar del Plata and Buenos Aires.
Won his first Yugoslav Championship (joint winner).
Became a World Championship Candidate after qualifying from the Amsterdam Interzonal.
Won his third Yugoslav Championship.
Died on February 14 in Belgrade, Serbia.

name: Gulnara Karimova
milestone_by_age_26: No independent material milestone by age 26; Karimova's career consisted of university degrees (BA from Tashkent State University, 1994) and early diplomatic internships while being the daughter of Uzbekistan's president. Her major appointments (UN representative, ambassador) came after age 30.
early_history_summary: Karimova graduated from Tashkent State University in 1994 with a BA in International Economics, completed a jewelry design course at FIT New York in 1992, and began diplomatic work in 1995 at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. She started at Harvard in 1998 for a master's degree. Her career was entirely facilitated by her father's position as president.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Islam Karimov, president of Uzbekistan from 1991 to 2016, and Tatyana Karimova; born into extreme political power and wealth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was the authoritarian ruler of Uzbekistan; Karimova's career opportunities were entirely derived from her father's political position.
evidence_summary: Karimova's early career was entirely facilitated by being the daughter of Uzbekistan's president. Her degrees, internships, and early diplomatic roles were not independently verifiable material milestones — they were products of nepotism rather than personal achievement. No material milestone by age 26 was found that was independent of her father's political power. She was later convicted of corruption and imprisoned.

name: Eduardo Souto de Moura
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Souto de Moura was still a student working as an assistant to Álvaro Siza. He received his architecture degree in 1980 at age 28 and won his first independent commission (Casa das Artes competition) the same year.
early_history_summary: Souto de Moura studied sculpture before switching to architecture at the School of Fine Arts of the University of Porto. From 1974 to 1979 he worked with Álvaro Siza Vieira at his architectural practice. He received his degree in 1980 and began his independent career that year after winning a design competition for the Casa das Artes in Porto.
family_context_summary: Son of medical doctor José Alberto Souto de Moura and Maria Teresa Ramos Machado; his brother was the former Attorney-General of Portugal.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a medical doctor; brother served as Attorney-General of Portugal, indicating an educated, professional family.
evidence_summary: Souto de Moura came from an educated Portuguese family (father a doctor, brother a future Attorney-General). He studied at the Porto School of Architecture and apprenticed under Álvaro Siza from 1974-1979, but did not complete his degree or win any independent commission until 1980 at age 28. No material milestone by age 26 was found; his Pritzker Prize came in 2011 at age 58.

name: Rosemarie Ackermann
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1974 European Championship gold medal in high jump at age 22, setting a world record of 1.95m, and later won the 1976 Olympic gold medal at age 24 and became the first woman to clear 2.00m at age 25.
early_history_summary: Ackermann (née Witschas) was born in Lohsa, Saxony, East Germany, and competed for SC Cottbus. She won the East German high jump championship in 1973 at age 21, competed in the 1972 Olympics at age 20 finishing seventh, then broke through internationally in 1974 by winning the European Championship in Rome with a world record of 1.95m.
family_context_summary: Born in Lohsa, Saxony, East Germany; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Ackermann benefited from the East German state sports system, which identified and developed athletic talent through specialized training from a young age. She competed for SC Cottbus and was East German champion by 1973 at age 21. Her European Championship gold in 1974 at age 22, with a world record of 1.95m, was a clear material milestone. She went on to win Olympic gold in 1976 and became the first woman to clear 2.00m in 1977. Family background is not documented, but the East German system provided elite coaching, facilities, and competitive infrastructure.
starting_point: Born in Lohsa, Saxony, East Germany; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from athletics since 1980; resides in Germany; last competed at the 1980 Olympics placing fourth.

trajectory.event: Competed at the Munich Olympics, finishing seventh in the high jump.
Won European Championship gold in Rome, setting a world record of 1.95m.
Won Olympic gold medal in the high jump at the Montreal Olympics.
Became the first woman in history to clear 2.00 metres in the high jump.
Won silver at the European Championships in Prague, losing her title to Sara Simeoni.
Placed fourth at the Moscow Olympics and retired from athletics.

name: Bang Si-hyuk
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest in 1994 at age 22, launching his professional songwriting career, and joined JYP Entertainment as a songwriter and producer in 1997 at age 25, co-producing hit songs for first-generation K-pop groups.
early_history_summary: Bang grew up in a musical home in Seoul and formed a band in middle school, writing and performing his own compositions. He studied aesthetics at Seoul National University, where he debuted as a composer. In 1994, he won the Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest, which launched his professional career. He met Park Jin-young in 1997 and joined JYP Entertainment as a songwriter and producer.
family_context_summary: Born in Seoul, South Korea; father was Bang Keuk-yoon, a notable figure. Grew up in a musical home but parents discouraged a music career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Bang Keuk-yoon was a notable public figure; family had musical interests but discouraged Bang from pursuing music professionally.
evidence_summary: Bang grew up in a musical household in Seoul and wrote songs from middle school, though his parents discouraged a music career. He studied aesthetics at Seoul National University, providing intellectual depth to his musical interests. Winning the Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest in 1994 at age 22 was a material milestone that launched his professional career. His partnership with Park Jin-young at JYP Entertainment from 1997 gave him mentorship, production infrastructure, and access to the emerging K-pop industry. He later founded Big Hit Entertainment in 2005 and created BTS, becoming a billionaire.
starting_point: Born in Seoul, South Korea; father was a notable public figure; grew up in a musical home with parents who discouraged a music career.
current_position: Chairman of HYBE Corporation; estimated net worth ~$3B; only billionaire in South Korean entertainment industry; stepped down as CEO in 2021.

trajectory.event: Won the Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest, launching his professional songwriting career.
Met Park Jin-young and joined JYP Entertainment as a songwriter and producer.
Co-produced hit songs for first-generation K-pop group g.o.d, earning the nickname 'Hitman Bang'.

Took Big Hit (renamed HYBE) public on the Korea Exchange, becoming a billionaire.

name: Kazuyoshi Miura
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Japan Soccer League title with Yomiuri SC in 1991-92 at age 24, and was named the inaugural J-League Most Valuable Player in 1993 at age 26, becoming the face of Japanese professional football.
early_history_summary: Miura left Shizuoka Gakuen High School after less than a year and traveled alone to Brazil at age 15 to become a professional footballer. He signed with the youth squad of Juventus-SP in São Paulo and turned professional with Santos in 1986 at age 19. After playing for several Brazilian clubs, he returned to Japan in 1990 and joined Yomiuri SC, winning consecutive JSL titles and then becoming the J-League's first MVP in 1993.
family_context_summary: Born in Shizuoka, Japan; family background not documented in reviewed sources. Left home at 15 to pursue football in Brazil.
evidence_summary: Miura's path was defined by extraordinary self-driven initiative: leaving school at 15 to travel alone to Brazil, the epicenter of world football, to train and play. This immersion in Brazilian football culture from age 15 to 23 gave him skills and experience unavailable in Japan at the time. Returning to Japan in 1990, he joined Yomiuri SC and won consecutive JSL titles, then became the inaugural J-League MVP in 1993 at age 26, riding the wave of Japanese football professionalization. Family background is not documented, but his trajectory reflects constraint-driven self-creation rather than inherited advantage.
starting_point: Born in Shizuoka, Japan; family background not documented in reviewed sources; left home at 15 to pursue football in Brazil.
current_position: Still playing professional football at age 59, on loan at Fukushima United from Yokohama FC; the world's oldest active professional footballer.

trajectory.event: Signed his first professional contract with Santos FC in Brazil.
Returned to Japan and joined Yomiuri SC, becoming a star in the Japan Soccer League.
Won the JSL title with Yomiuri, the last JSL championship before the J-League era.
Named the inaugural J-League Most Valuable Player and won the J-League title with Verdy Kawasaki.
Loaned to Genoa in Italy's Serie A, becoming one of the first Japanese players in a top European league.
Still playing professionally, on loan at Fukushima United, holding the record as the world's oldest active professional footballer.

name: Tetsuo Okamoto
milestone_by_age_26: Won two gold medals (400m and 1500m freestyle) and a silver (4x200m relay) at the inaugural 1951 Pan American Games at age 19, and won Olympic bronze in the 1500m freestyle at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age 20.
early_history_summary: Okamoto was born in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil to parents of Japanese heritage. He began swimming at age 7 to treat asthma, but only began serious training at age 15 when coach Fausto Alonso arrived to form a team at Yara Clube in Marília. He became Brazilian champion in 1950 at age 18, set South American records in January 1951, and won two gold medals at the 1951 Pan American Games at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil to parents of Japanese heritage; family background otherwise not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were of Japanese heritage living in Brazil.
evidence_summary: Okamoto began swimming at age 7 to treat asthma, a health constraint that catalyzed his athletic career. At 15, coach Fausto Alonso arrived in his hometown and provided serious training, transforming Okamoto into a competitive swimmer. He became Brazilian champion at 18, set South American records at 19, and won two Pan American gold medals in 1951. His Olympic bronze in 1952 was the first swimming medal in Brazilian history. The combination of a health-driven early start, a dedicated coach, and natural talent drove his rapid ascent. Family background beyond Japanese-Brazilian heritage is not documented.
starting_point: Born in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil to parents of Japanese heritage; began swimming at age 7 to treat asthma.
current_position: Died October 1, 2007 at age 75 in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil; final role: retired swimmer and former Olympic medalist.

trajectory.event: Became Brazilian swimming champion for the first time.
Won two gold medals and a silver at the inaugural Pan American Games in Buenos Aires.
Won Olympic bronze in the 1500m freestyle at Helsinki, the first swimming medal in Brazilian history.
Swam for Texas A&M University in the United States, becoming a four-time All-American.
Died on October 1 in Marília, São Paulo, Brazil.

name: Jostein Gaarder
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Gaarder graduated from the University of Oslo in 1976 and was working as a high school teacher. His first notable published work, The Solitaire Mystery, came in 1990 at age 38.
early_history_summary: Gaarder was born in Oslo, Norway, to a school headmaster father and a teacher/children's book author mother. He attended the Oslo Cathedral School and studied Scandinavian languages and theology at the University of Oslo, graduating in 1976. He then worked as a high school teacher in Bergen before beginning his literary career.
family_context_summary: Born in Oslo, Norway; father was a school headmaster and mother Inger Margrethe Gaarder was a teacher and author of children's books.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a teacher and children's book author; father was a school headmaster — both were in education and literature, providing a literary household environment.
evidence_summary: Gaarder grew up in a literary household — his father was a school headmaster and his mother was a teacher and children's book author. He studied Scandinavian languages and theology at the University of Oslo and graduated in 1976 at age 24, then became a high school teacher. No published literary work or material milestone by age 26 was found. His breakthrough novel, The Solitaire Mystery, was published in 1990 when he was 38, and Sophie's World followed in 1991 to massive international success.

name: Rodrigo Valdez
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26; Valdez had a professional boxing record of approximately 30+ fights by age 26 but had not won any championship title. His first title (NABF middleweight) came in September 1973 at age 27, and his first world title (WBC middleweight) in May 1974 at age 28.
early_history_summary: Valdez began his professional boxing career on October 25, 1963 at age 17 in Cartagena, Colombia. He won his first nine bouts before losing to Rudy Escobar in 1965. He fought primarily in Colombia through the 1960s, then moved to the United States in 1969-1970 to campaign in New York, Nevada, and California. He fought at Madison Square Garden in 1971 but did not win a championship until 1973.
family_context_summary: Born in Cartagena, Colombia (Bolívar department); family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Valdez turned professional at 17 in 1963 and fought extensively in Colombia through the 1960s, then moved to the US in 1969-1970 to gain recognition. While he had many professional fights and fought at Madison Square Garden by age 25, no championship or material title milestone by age 26 was found. His first title (NABF middleweight) came in September 1973 at age 27, and his WBC world middleweight title came in May 1974 at age 28. Family background is not documented.
